clue.text: Hear cuckoo and another bird

indicators.note: cuckoo here means crazy, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher hears a cuckoo call and then spots a second bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the first bird, making 'another bird' read naturally; in fact it is the anagram signal for HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird, related to the ostrich and emu.

clue.text: Sushi on ice, a strange item of oriental cuisine

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters before it form something odd, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sushi served on ice is an odd dish from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweet, thick soybean condiment is a staple of Chinese cooking, an oriental food item.

clue.text: A new betting hint regarding course leader

parts.note: a tip is advice on which horse to back
as to means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A fresh racing tip about the horse leading the field on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a racecourse, fitting the betting; here it is a course of a meal, the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian starter of cold meats and vegetables is the first course of a meal, so it leads the courses.

clue.text: WASP, say, taking the vote of a Conservative after dockers have struck twice?

indicators.note: to dock is to cut short, and two strikes mean two words each lose their final letter

parts.note: to poll people is to take their votes
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A sly political sketch: a WASP voter canvassing a Tory after a double dock strike.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLING A TORY is docked twice, losing the G of POLLING and the Y of TORY. WASP in capitals suggests the American social label, but here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps carry pollen between flowers as they feed, so a wasp is one example of a pollen carrier.

clue.text: Move round City in a mass of people

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for a crowd

parts.note: a press is a crowd of people pushing together
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone moves around the city among a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To precess is to rotate in a way that the axis of spin itself turns, as a top or the Earth does.

clue.text: Oh, OK, owl goes round hunting but are you any different?

indicators.note: the letters go round and come out in a different order

parts.note: stalking is hunting prey by stealth

explanation.surface: An owl on the hunt is told by an onlooker that it is no better than they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a retort: the phrase is said to a critic guilty of the same fault.
explanation.definitionFit: The retort is aimed at critics with the same fault, effectively asking whether they are any better.

clue.text: French police officer cuts interior visit

indicators.note: the officer's word cuts into the abbreviation, splitting it

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A French gendarme shortens an inland trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visit' suggests a trip; it is the old sense of visiting a punishment on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit suffering upon someone is an old phrase meaning to impose or deal it out.

clue.text: Thin material in Cicero cut over English

indicators.note: in a down clue the shortened name sits over, above, the letter for English
the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Tully was the traditional English name for Marcus Tullius Cicero

explanation.surface: A flimsy fabric appears in a Cicero text cut for an English edition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine netting of silk or nylon used for veils and tutus is a thin fabric.

clue.text: Girl embracing golf as a game

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps around the letter

parts.note: Ruby is a girl's name
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl takes up golf as her sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' looks like the game being defined; it is only the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: The football game played with an oval ball is named after the English school where it began.

clue.text: Go mad with support for musical fiddler after stroke

indicators.note: the stroke is placed first, with the support coming after it

parts.note: to hit something is to strike or stroke it
the musical Fiddler on the Roof has its fiddler supported by a rooftop

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper after a violinist in a musical is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for erupting in sudden fury is a common way of saying someone has gone mad with anger.

clue.text: Dog runs round large seal

indicators.note: the dog's name encircles the abbreviation that follows it

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A dog runs circles around a big seal on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' suggests the marine animal next to the dog; it is the verb or noun meaning a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper that closes a hole or bath outlet acts as a seal; to stop up a gap is to seal it.

clue.text: Briefly went in water outside English Channel resort

indicators.note: the shortened word sits around the single letter for English
said briefly, the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to dip is to go briefly into water

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker took a quick swim at an English seaside town on the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the last letter of DIPPED to give DIPPE, and 'outside' puts that round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French port and seaside town on the English Channel coast of Normandy.

clue.text: Bearded grain produce Queen is into

indicators.note: the royal abbreviation goes inside the spirit, as if the Queen were into it

parts.note: whisky is distilled from grain such as barley
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a common abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A bearded farmer is keen on the spirit his grain makes, and so is the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is into' reads as the Queen being fond of a dram, but it is a containment signal: the royal abbreviation sits inside the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiskers are facial hair, so a face covered in them is bearded or bristly.

clue.text: Understand embassy is allowing visitors back in?

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that an embassy is letting its guests return.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting people in again after they have left is the act of re-entry permission, so a question mark fits.

clue.text: Isaiah represents divinity

parts.note: Is is the standard abbreviation for the biblical book of Isaiah
to represent something is to be it, as in 'this is the plan'

explanation.surface: A theological statement that the prophet Isaiah stands for the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, so she is a divinity.

clue.text: Promise to hide drinks in football kit?

indicators.note: the promise conceals the drinks within itself

parts.note: to swear is to promise solemnly
ports are fortified wines from Portugal

explanation.surface: Players vow to conceal their drinks inside their football strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing designed for games and athletics covers football kit, so the kit is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Friday even, for example, could be a little cavalier

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a cavalier was a mounted knight or horseman

explanation.surface: A small Royalist cavalier might appear on a Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' looks like the adverb; here it is the old word for evening, so Friday even is Friday evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday evening falls in the working week, an example of an evening Monday to Friday.

clue.text: Praising European Union planning in detail?

parts.note: logistics is the detailed planning of an operation, so the adjective describes it

explanation.surface: Someone admires the EU's meticulous planning.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of praise, so the adjective formed from it means full of praise.

clue.text: Cause of blast, perhaps one key US gunpowder ingredient

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is a musical key
niter is the American spelling of nitre, saltpetre, used in gunpowder

explanation.surface: An essential American gunpowder component could set off an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sets off a charge or fuel is what causes an explosion to happen.

clue.text: Stylish range in yellow

parts.note: chic means stylish
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A fashionable collection in a yellow colourway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' reads as a colour; it is slang for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and a coward is often called by the farmyard bird's name.

clue.text: Adapted for radio a while ago, Mann's first novel

definitions.text: Adapted for radio a while ago, Mann's first
definitions.meaning: in the old British signallers' spelling alphabet the letter M, first of Mann
Jane Austen's novel about a matchmaking heiress

explanation.surface: A Thomas Mann first novel was once dramatised on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a radio adaptation of Thomas Mann's debut; actually the old signals alphabet, as in 'ack emma' for a.m., used this name for M.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's 1815 book about Miss Woodhouse is one of the best-known English novels.

clue.text: Given mission to enter cell, avoiding outside guard

parts.note: someone given a mission has been sent out
to enter is to go in

indicators.note: the word's outer letters are skipped, leaving only its interior

explanation.surface: A prisoner is assigned the task of entering a cell while keeping clear of the exterior guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier posted to keep watch, which is a synonym for a guard.

clue.text: Faces second date in Rome

parts.note: the Ides was a date in the ancient Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: Faces seen on a second date in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The faces of a cube or building are its flat surfaces, also called its sides.

clue.text: Peruvian city's zoo originally in area to preserve, on reflection

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the city to its wordplay

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, the letters are read backwards
the zoo's first letter goes inside the area and preserve letters

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins

indicators.note: originally means the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A Peruvian city's zoo was first set up in a conservation area.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazca is a city in southern Peru, famous for the giant Nazca Lines drawn in the desert.

clue.text: A little exhibition is expected to charge

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small show is supposed to cost something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to charge' reads as setting a price for admission; it is the physics sense of giving atoms an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn atoms into ions is to give them an electrical charge, a physics synonym.

clue.text: Sleep, and rise finally after twelve?

indicators.note: the letter from rise is placed after the abbreviation for twelve

parts.note: doz is the abbreviation for ..., a set of twelve

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A question of whether to nap and then get up after midnight or noon.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off lightly for a short time is a light form of sleep.

clue.text: Muslim chief in fine family is to have another brood?

parts.note: thin means fine, as in fine thread

indicators.note: the chief's title goes inside the pair of words for fine and family

parts.note: kin are one's family
an aga is a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A Muslim leader in a slender family wonders whether to have more children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' looks like a family of young, matching 'family'; here it is the verb meaning to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to ponder at length, so another brood is reconsidering a matter.

clue.text: Plant boy's brought round moved grandpa

indicators.note: the boy's word is placed around the shuffled letters

parts.note: a son is a boy, the 's standing for has

indicators.note: moved means the letters of grandpa are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's son has wheeled his grandfather round to the flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The antirrhinum is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: River central to Chatham dockyards and Rochester

indicators.note: the middle letter of each of the four following words is taken

explanation.surface: A river runs through the middle of the Kent dockyards at Chatham and Rochester.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the Medway, the river at Chatham and Rochester in Kent; the answer is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne flows through Newcastle in north-east England, so it is a river.
